classification.reason: The coach gives actionable instructions for players who get tight in big moments to swing harder/faster, modify targeting toward court center, and aggressively transition forward to the net.

problem.title_as_question: How can you choke-proof your game when experiencing anxiety in big moments?
problem.definition: Under pressure, anxiety commonly triggers a freeze or flight response leading to muscle tightness, tentativeness, missed shots, and passive positioning behind the baseline.
prerequisites: transitioning to net and hitting volleys
problem.target_player: players who get tight or tentative in big moments

symptoms.description: Missing shots long due to tension in the forearms and upper body slowing down the swing and opening the racket face.
Recovering sideways or waiting behind the baseline without explosive footwork in a passive survival mindset.
Tentative feeling and hesitation during shot execution and forward movement when under pressure.

causes.statement: Anxiety causes an involuntary freeze response that introduces tension in the forearms and upper body, making the racket swing slower and open up.
A psychological flight or freeze response leads players to recover passively to the side and wait behind the baseline instead of moving forward.
Remaining at the baseline after hitting an aggressive shot gives the opponent extra seconds to recover and forces the hitter to produce multiple additional winners.

angles.summary: Tension in the forearm and upper body mechanically slows down racket rotation and leaves the face slightly open at contact, causing shots to sail long.
Sinner increased his average forehand speed from 82 mph to 88 mph in the final games of Wimbledon to forcibly trigger a fight response.
Taking the ball at the net takes away two to three seconds of recovery time from the opponent and turns difficult defensive shots into trivial putaways.
Achieving true outcome independence means accepting that the opponent might play too well, freeing you to sprint and commit with zero hesitation.

solutions.summary: Tell yourself to swing harder and swing faster in big moments to guide yourself into a fight response and override tension.
Aim down the absolute center of that half of the court rather than flirting with the lines when ripping big-moment groundstrokes.
solutions.external_goal: center of that half of the court

solutions.summary: Practice recovering forward toward the baseline, split-stepping forward into the court, and sprinting up to hit the ball at its apex.
Sprint forward and fully commit to the net without hesitation after attacking, forcing your opponent to produce a miracle passing shot.
Adopt complete outcome independence by accepting that you might lose if the opponent hits too well, allowing you to play all-out without hesitation.
